lines.text: Mezo's MUSD savings rate moves. About five percent in April. About thirteen percent last week.
If you save in MUSD, you can't plan around that. Tenor lets you lock it.
Tenor puts your MUSD into Mezo's savings vault, sMUSD, and splits it in two.
PT is worth exactly one MUSD at maturity. YT receives all the yield until then.
This is Tenor, live on Mezo Testnet. The fixed rate sits right next to what sMUSD actually paid on mainnet.
To fix my yield, I enter an amount and Tenor quotes the PT I get, and what it's worth on December thirty-first.
One click, one transaction. The return is locked the moment I buy.
The green line is my fixed path. The grey band is where the variable rate could land.
Or the other way round: keep the deposit as PT, sell the future yield, and get MUSD today.
Every action is a single transaction through Mezo's concentrated liquidity pools, with quotes that match the router to the wei.
Real Mezo protocol yield has already flowed through YT: forty-one MUSD, claimed on-chain.
And for BTC borrowers: Mezo lends MUSD at a fixed one percent. Put it into PT, and the whole spread is fixed.
Verified contracts, twenty-nine tests, and every action proven on-chain.
